newsitem.title: USA: BZW Securities economist sees further UK rate rise.
newsitem.headline: BZW Securities economist sees further UK rate rise.

text.p: Official UK interest rates will likely head even higher this year to keep the economy from expanding too rapidly, according to Chris Iggo, chief economist at BZW Securities Inc.
On Tuesday, Britain's new Labour government hiked official rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent and gave the Bank of England (BOE) operational responsibility for setting rates.

"The economy in the U.K. is growing quite quickly," said Iggo during a speech here to members of the British-American Chamber of Commerce. Iggo contended interest rates will probably rise further over the next six months.
Iggo said raising UK interest rates is probably the most effective means in the near term to control inflation.
But he said raising rates could push the exchange rate even higher and that would be a problem for exporters.
Indeed, the pound rallied to more than 4-1/2 year highs on Tuesday after news of the rate hike and greater freedom for the BOE to set monetary policy.
Iggo noted that a recent newspaper article warned a further rise in the pound now runs a risk of a sharp drop in the pound in a few months' time.
"If EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) is on the agenda, then the government will want less exchange rate volatility not more," Iggo said.
"So, there has to be some concern about how the foreign exchange markets will respond to this early tightening of monetary policy," he said.
